chunks: Thus in varied ways We explain Our signs so that they may say: 'You have been instructed,' and that We might make it clear to those who understand.

key_terms.لِنُبَيِّنَهُ: That We may make it clear

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah vary the presentation of signs in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the variation of signs (takhfif wa tashdid) is viewed as a divine pedagogical strategy to accommodate different levels of intellectual capacity, ensuring that the message remains accessible yet profound. The term 'darasa' (studied/learned) highlights the tension between the Prophet's innate prophetic status and the external perception of his learning, while 'qawmin ya'lamun' refers specifically to those with deep spiritual insight who can discern the deeper truths behind the apparent simplicity. This verse underscores the Shia emphasis on the necessity of both outward transmission and inward comprehension for true understanding of the Quran.
